title: Reserved-pool warmup suppression heuristic gap causing enterprise burst shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced sustained 5-15% request shedding during micro-bursts on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10 despite reserved pool headroom. Initial alerts showed burst credits available but warmup_allocator suppressed reservation growth for tenants labelled as 'conservative-warmup'. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfix rollout, customer comms, and long-term mitigations.
root_cause: The warmup admission controller used a conservative decay window when computing tenant warmup scores. Under a pattern of repeated short bursts from high-cardinality tenant sets, the controller suppressed new reserved leases because it believed the tenant was still cooling down. Combined with an edge case in the burst-credit reconciliation where partial preemptions left stale headroom markers, the scheduler refused to allocate available cold-pool slots to the affected tenants for up to 90s, causing request shedding even though physical GPU capacity existed.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-12: loosen warmup suppression threshold for tenants with enterprise SLA label, add immediate lease override when burst-credit > 80% and physical slot availability detected, and added a short-circuit to bypass decay checks for requests with VIP routing. Hotfix rollout staged across regions (us-east-1 then eu-west-1) with canary metrics. Customer-facing Q/A and edge-case fallback policy enabled while stable.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial alerting spike from Monitoring. Two enterprise customers (AcmePayments, MacroHealth) reported increased 429/503 across short bursts. Pager duty routed to infra-oncall.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Kim: Reproduced local repro with synthetic burst generator. Observed warmup_score not decaying as expected when bursts are high-frequency; tenant label gating respected conservative policy leading to suppressed allocations.
2026-03-11 - Lina Gomez (SRE): Added temporary override rule in admission-controller config; created emergency rollout plan. Noted potential for noisy allocations, monitoring added.

2026-03-12 - Daniel Kim: Deployed hotfix (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6678). Canary passed in us-east-1. Increased allocation events for affected tenants; error-rate returned to baseline for AcmePayments.
2026-03-13 - PM sync: Comms draft prepared for affected customers; operations to run additional soak tests in eu-west-1 before full rollout.
2026-03-14 - Post-hotfix telemetry: 95th percentile allocation latency down by 60ms; burst-shed rate reduced to <0.1% for customers previously impacted. Preparing full postmortem.
2026-03-14 - Note from QA: Integration test added to ensure warmup suppression bypass triggers when lease-override active (test id: integ-warmup-001)
playbook_changes: - Add a lease-override emergency action to the dedicated autoscaler playbook for enterprise-tier tenants.\n- Include a runbook section to validate stale headroom markers and a manual reconciliation step.\n- Add telemetry checks to detect warmup_score plateau lasting >60s during repeated bursts.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-2146802 - Implement long-term warmup predictor that uses burst frequency histogram instead of single decay window
ENG-2146803 - Reconcile and prune stale headroom markers in reconciliation job; add unit tests
ENG-2146804 - Add e2e chaos test that simulates high-cardinality micro-bursts against reserved pools
ENG-2146805 - Customer outreach: one-to-one debrief with AcmePayments & MacroHealth; offer dedicated postmortem call
comms_template:
Subject: Incident summary — temporary capacity shortfall and mitigation

Hi <Customer-Team>,

We detected a temporary capacity shortfall affecting a subset of enterprise customers between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-12. Root cause: a conservative warmup suppression heuristic prevented timely allocation of reserved slots during rapid, repeated micro-bursts.

What we did: applied a targeted hotfix to bypass suppression for enterprise SLA tenants, performed staged rollouts, and validated traffic returned to normal.

Impact: brief request shedding for a small portion of traffic (estimated <2% of requests during peak micro-bursts).

Next steps: permanent heuristic improvements, additional testing, and a debrief call if desired.

Apologies for the disruption — we take these incidents seriously and are prioritizing follow-up work.

Best,
Redwood Inference Operations
rollback_plan: If allocation regressions observed after hotfix, immediate rollback steps: 1) revert PR 6678 (github revert procedure), 2) re-enable previous admission-controller config, 3) scale up temporary dedicated cold-pool by +10% capacity in affected region, 4) notify customers via incident channel. Rollback tested in staging 2026-03-12.
notes: Unique aspects: this issue surfaced only for high-cardinality tenant patterns combined with enterprise label gating. Preventing recurrence requires both scheduler policy changes and improved telemetry to detect the specific signature (warmup plateau + stale headroom markers).
customer_updates: 2026-03-12 - Sent initial targeted notification to AcmePayments and MacroHealth describing mitigation and timeline.
2026-03-14 - Follow-up with technical postmortem and offer of a joint review call.
2026-03-15 - Customer success to confirm SLA credits if requested and track any downstream impact.
